items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Terminology 36:1
items.html: Time, motion, and place are almost one matter, for they are relations of change and renewal of form, as written above in Part 1, p. 26, in the Inner Observation. However, when the discussion concerns the orders of the cascading of the degrees, the changes are regarded as places; and when the discussion is from the aspect of cause and consequence, they are regarded in orders of time. (p. 616, Item 22)
